title: C Programming Foundations
subtitle: Build the C memory model needed for real data structures.
description: A cumulative introduction to C execution, control flow, functions, arrays, pointers, structs, dynamic memory, multi-file design, and deterministic testing.
audience: Learners following the cumulative C data-structures and algorithms pathway.
prerequisites: Basic comfort using a browser-based editor.
goals: Trace C execution and memory state.
Use pointers, structs, and dynamic memory with explicit ownership.
Build and test a cumulative record-management project.

teachingStyle.tone: Visual, precise, book-like, cumulative, and implementation-focused.

animationRules: Use previous, next, play or pause, replay, and a visible step counter.
Keep layouts stable; animate links, active cells, call frames, or edges rather than moving the whole structure.
Synchronize heap tree and array states, recursion and call stack states, and graph state with queue or stack state.
Prefer five to ten meaningful frames and one state transition per frame.
pseudocodeRules: Use dialect zoeskoul-v1 and inputKind pseudocode_input.
Accept equivalent variable names and harmless syntax variants after normalization.
Require explicit termination, state updates, and invariant-preserving branches.
Use structure plus scenario execution for pass/fail.
Keep the learner pseudocode visible beside the following C translation exercise.
workspaceRules: Reuse the same course workspace across module projects.
Do not ask learners to create boilerplate files or remember compiler commands.
Each new module adds focused .h/.c files while preserving prior passing tests.
Project steps are progressive and may not reset earlier work.
